title: Google launches Gemini 4 Carbon with a ‘significant leap’ in cybersecurity
content:
Google has released its latest frontier model, Gemini 4 Carbon, offering “significant gains” in coding, agentic tasks, and cybersecurity. In an announcement on Wednesday, Google highlights Carbon’s top spot on the Artificial Analysis Intelligence Index (v5.0) benchmark, with Claude Opus 5.5 and GPT-6 Astra trailing behind.
Google launches Gemini 4 Carbon with a ‘significant leap’ in cybersecurity
Gemini 4 Carbon is outperforming the top models from OpenAI and Anthropic on some benchmarks.
The new Gemini 4 Carbon model offers improvements over Argon, which Google released earlier this month. It’s currently only available to a select group of cybersecurity defense companies, but it will eventually expand to other partners in its Fairwind Program.
The company says Carbon reflects the “pace at which we’re pushing the frontier forward,” coming with a “significant leap” in cyberdefense that makes it better at finding vulnerabilities and generating secure code. Carbon currently holds the number one spot on SEC-bench Pro, a benchmark that measures an AI model’s ability to discover real-world bugs, and ExploitGym, which measures how a model can turn a vulnerability into exploits.
Google says Gemini 4 Carbon is built for completing longer tasks, adding that its internal teams have seen it “run for days to persist through dead ends to tackle complex, multi-step engineering tasks.” It’s also better at avoiding shortcuts, resisting prompt injection attacks, and collaborating with users, according to Google. Carbon is supposed to offer more “transparency and honesty” as well, by cutting “unsupported claims” by two times when compared to Argon.
It will launch at the same competitive introductory price as Argon, at $2 per million input tokens and $10 per million output tokens.

report.summary: Google releases Gemini 4 Carbon, a frontier AI model claiming significant gains in coding, agentic tasks, and cybersecurity, topping benchmarks and initially available to select cyberdefense firms.
report.background: The launch lands in an intensifying race among Google, OpenAI, and Anthropic to build ever more capable frontier models. Cybersecurity has become a key proving ground because AI can both find and exploit software vulnerabilities, making secure-code generation and bug discovery high-stakes tests of model usefulness. Google previously released Gemini Argon earlier this month, and Carbon is a faster follow-up. Access is deliberately limited to a select group of cybersecurity defense companies through Google’s Fairwind Program, reflecting cautious deployment of dual-use capabilities. The article cites benchmark positions on Artificial Analysis Intelligence Index v5.0, SEC-bench Pro, and ExploitGym, and says Carbon will launch at the same introductory price as Argon: $2 per million input tokens and $10 per million output tokens.
key_points: Benchmark leadership: Google says Gemini 4 Carbon tops the Artificial Analysis Intelligence Index v5.0, ahead of Claude Opus 5.5 and GPT-6 Astra. It also holds the No. 1 spot on SEC-bench Pro, which measures real-world bug discovery, and ExploitGym, which tests turning vulnerabilities into exploits.

Cybersecurity leap: Carbon is described as significantly better at finding vulnerabilities and generating secure code. Its initial release is restricted to selected cybersecurity defense companies via the Fairwind Program, with broader partner access expected later.

Long-running agentic work: Google says Carbon is built for complex, multi-step engineering tasks and can run for days, persisting through dead ends. It is also better at avoiding shortcuts, resisting prompt injection, and collaborating with users, according to the company.
More honest outputs: Carbon reportedly cuts unsupported claims by two times compared with Argon, part of a push for greater transparency and reliability in model responses.
Pricing and access: Carbon will launch at the same competitive introductory price as Argon, $2 per million input tokens and $10 per million output tokens, though availability remains limited for now.
report.impact: For the AI industry, Gemini 4 Carbon raises the competitive bar on coding, agentic reliability, and cybersecurity benchmarks, pushing rivals to respond on both capability and safety. For developers, the model promises stronger secure-code generation and long-running task persistence, plus better prompt-injection resistance, but limited access means most will wait for broader availability. The attractive token pricing could pressure competitors. For regular users, the clearest benefit is indirect: AI that helps defenders find bugs faster could make software safer, while the same dual-use capabilities also raise concerns about AI-assisted cyberattacks. Google’s staged rollout signals that frontier cyber models will likely be released carefully, with trusted partners first and broader access later.
report.tools: To follow related work, watch AI cybersecurity and secure-coding tools such as OWASP ZAP and Semgrep for vulnerability scanning, GitHub CodeQL and Snyk for secure code analysis, and Garak or PromptInject for LLM red-teaming and prompt-injection testing. Google’s Gemini API and Fairwind Program are worth monitoring for future access, while SEC-bench Pro and ExploitGym offer benchmark context for evaluating cyber-capable models.
